citation: Bond, Francis, and Joanna Ut-Seong Sio. 2024. A Construction-based Approach to Cantonese Classifiers. Proceedings of the 31st International Conference on Head-Driven Phrase Structure Grammar, 60–75.
profile: Cantonese D-(X)-C-N, X-C-N, and C-N noun phrases
verified_claim: Directly distinguishes definite D-(X)-C-N, indefinite X-C-N, and (in)definite C-N; gives exact D-(one)-C-N with the numeral optional; models D-X-C-N and D-C-N separately; assigns no-numeral classifier phrases semantic cardinality one.
limitation: Cardinality one is a semantic analysis, not permission to insert an unpronounced numeral into the surface tree. The HPSG structure and cognitive-status mapping are one analysis and should not be made parser truth without comparison.

citation: Cheng, Lisa Lai-Shen, and Rint Sybesma. 2014. The Syntactic Structure of Noun Phrases. In The Handbook of Chinese Linguistics, 248–274.
profile: Cantonese demonstrative, numeral, classifier, noun order and ellipsis
verified_claim: States the unmarked order Dem–Numeral–Classifier–Modifier–N; demonstrates that a Cantonese demonstrative may omit the numeral but must be followed by a classifier; treats Cantonese C-N as common without requiring a covert numeral; records noun ellipsis after a classifier; summarizes [Dem (Nume) Cl N] as a core profile.
limitation: The chapter compares multiple syntactic theories and does not provide a complete lexical classifier–noun compatibility inventory. Its no-covert-numeral claim concerns structure and need not conflict with a semantic cardinality-one analysis.

citation: Matthews, Stephen, and Virginia Yip. Cantonese: A Comprehensive Grammar, multimedia Chapter 6, The noun phrase.
locator: Sections 6.1.1–6.2.4 and 6.3.2; exact examples 嗰張檯, 呢間學校, 呢件事, 呢位同事, and 你嗰個朋友
profile: Headed demonstrative-classifier noun phrases and classifier subtypes
verified_claim: Directly attests multiple no-numeral Dem-CL-N phrases with sortal, human, and abstract-noun classifiers and separately illustrates classifier-noun, measure/quantity classifier, alternative-classifier, and possessive-classifier structures.
limitation: The edited examples establish occurrence and useful contrasts but do not define a binary universal compatibility table or prove that every item labeled CL has the same syntax.

citation: Xia, Hengliang. 2025. Syntax of Classifiers and Measure Words in Chinese and Beyond. PhD thesis, University of Ottawa.
verified_claim: Reports grammaticality-judgement evidence for a systematic syntactic distinction in Cantonese: classifiers use a right-branching structure, while Cantonese measure words use a left-branching structure; argues that they are categorially and structurally distinct.
limitation: The current review could verify the official abstract but not retrieve the repository PDF through the connected reader. Do not cite unverified page-level examples or use the abstract alone to classify individual ambiguous lexemes.

citation: Tse, Shek Kam, Hui Li, and Shing On Leung. 2007. The acquisition of Cantonese classifiers by preschool children in Hong Kong. Journal of Child Language 34(3):495–517.
locator: Classifier typology and discussion of go3 general-classifier use
profile: Documents a complex Cantonese classifier inventory and reports that children strongly prefer general go3; the study argues that go3 can replace many sortal classifiers but not mensural classifiers, while specific classifier knowledge develops gradually.
verified_claim: Child-production preferences do not by themselves determine adult grammaticality. Overuse, default choice, and context-sensitive alternatives show why a single hard incompatibility list is too strong.

citation: Erbaugh, Mary S. 2013. Classifier choices in discourse across the seven main Chinese dialects. In Increased Empiricism: Recent Advances in Chinese Linguistics, 101–126.
profile: Reports that general classifiers dominate Cantonese discourse, Cantonese sortals are less frequent, and synonymous or alternative sortals are common; classifier choice varies across speakers and dialects.
verified_claim: Discourse frequencies do not erase lexical selection or establish that every general-classifier substitution is equally natural in every register and construction.

citation: Nagy, Naomi, and Samuel Lo. 2019. Classifier use in Heritage and Hong Kong Cantonese. Asia-Pacific Language Variation 5(1).
locator: Spontaneous heritage and Hong Kong Cantonese comparison
profile: Finds both heritage and homeland speakers strongly prefer general and mass classifiers and that classifier choice is primarily governed by noun number; documents specialization of go3 toward singular nouns.
verified_claim: Population-level variation and grammaticalization trends do not supply an item-level compatibility decision for a particular Dem-CL-N candidate.
